title: Cells and Body Systems

standard_code: Grade 9 Natural Sciences: Cells as the basic units of life; systems in the human body
standard_text: Cells are the basic units of life; plant and animal cells have structures such as the cell membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus, and plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole. Cells form tissues, organs and systems. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 9, Life and Living: Cells as the basic units of life; systems in the human body)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): plant and animal cells, cell structures and functions, microscopes, tissues, organs and organ systems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.
body_html:
How to think about it

All living things are made of cells. Animal and plant cells both have a cell membrane, cytoplasm, a nucleus and mitochondria. Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

Similar cells form tissues (muscle tissue), tissues form organs (the heart) and organs work together in systems (the circulatory system). The human body has skeletal, muscular, digestive, circulatory, respiratory, excretory, nervous, endocrine and reproductive systems.

Example

Which structure controls the cell?

It contains DNA.

Answer: the nucleus

Example

Which cell has chloroplasts: a leaf cell or a cheek cell?

Where does photosynthesis happen?

Answer: a leaf cell

Common mistakes

  • Thinking animal cells have cell walls.
  • Mixing up organs and tissues.
  • Thinking cells are the same size as the organism.
